history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2133 ('Shiv Bari Temple (Laleshwar Mahadev Mandir)', Bikaner) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 2067 ('Shiv Bari Temple', id 'shiv-bari-temple-bikaner') - the same temple: Laleshwar Mahadev Mandir is the local name of the Shiv Bari Temple. Deduplicate downstream. Built by Maharaja Doongar Singh (Dungar Singh) of Bikaner in 1880 CE to commemorate his father Maharaja Lal Singh - hence the local name 'Laleshwar Mahadev'. It is a virtual museum of Bikaner miniature paintings, with red-sandstone domes, pavilions and decorated columns behind a huge fortified embattlement wall. The main attraction is the four-faced idol of Lord Shiva carved in black marble (one source instead calls it one of India's largest Shiva lingas - flagging the discrepancy); a bronze Nandi faces it, two colossal bawaris (reservoirs) stand in the campus, and the exterior has statues of Krishna with the gopis. Date conflicts: a few low-quality sources say 1846, or the 18th century under Zorawar Singh - the majority of sources, including a 2024 Bikaner architecture journal paper, attribute the temple to Doongar Singh in the late 19th century; using 1880 CE.

name: Shiv Bari Temple (Laleshwar Mahadev Mandir)
town_description: Bikaner, founded in 1488 by Rao Bika of the Rathore clan, is a historic desert city in northwest Rajasthan famed for the unconquered Junagarh Fort, Lalgarh Palace, its camel-breeding farm, bhujia and old-city havelis; it is a major rail and road hub in the Thar region.

travel.road: New Shiv Bari Main Road, ~6 km from the city centre; local transport and autos readily available.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM - 7:00 PM (trawell.in). Mahashivratri and Shravan draw large crowds - visit early on festival days.
